title: The Chandelier Cluster, NGC 6723
caption: The globular cluster NGC 6723, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6723, the Chandelier Cluster · constellation Sagittarius · about 27,000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, A. Sarajedini, G. Piotto

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Month, June 2026 (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Like a chandelier, this ball of stars is full of lights, and each little bulb is a star. NGC 6723, sometimes nicknamed the Chandelier Cluster, is a globular cluster about 27,000 light-years away in Sagittarius, the Archer.

Globular clusters are dense groups of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity, and astronomers know of more than 150 in the Milky Way. They hold some of our galaxy’s oldest stars, often more than 10 billion years old, and may be among its first structures, formed long before the thin disc where the Sun orbits.

Astronomers once thought all of a cluster’s stars were born together. Hubble showed it is more complicated. Studying NGC 6723 in ultraviolet light, a team found signs of two bursts of star formation, the second within 634 million years of the first. For a cluster over 10 billion years old, that is a short gap.
scale: Using the source’s listed field of view (3.38 × 3.4 arcminutes) and its distance of about 27,000 light-years, the frame spans roughly 27 × 27 light-years. Its light set out about 27,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble’s cameras through five filters, from ultraviolet (275 nm) to near-infrared (814 nm). The color assigned to each filter isn’t published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the colors are assigned, so the eye would not see this palette.

explore: Hubble first imaged NGC 6723 in a survey of 65 Milky Way globular clusters, which has inspired several hundred research papers. A later program revisited many of them in ultraviolet light to pick out small chemical differences between stars.
alt: A dense, round swarm of thousands of stars in white, blue and gold, thinning toward the edges of a dark field.
